cases.contract_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant. Synthetic facts for this diagnostic only: the dwelling is within Urbana city limits; this is an ordinary residential tenancy entered in 2026, and none of the supplied Chapter 12.5 section 2 exclusions applies. These are stipulated test facts, not a real boundary lookup. Tenant agrees to repair identified housing-code violations in exchange for a rent reduction. This is a recital in a form lease; no bargaining evidence is supplied.
cases.criterion: Preserve knowing/intentional election, actual bargaining and the landlord proof burden; a form recital alone is insufficient.
must_not_infer: Do not treat the form recital as conclusive proof of bargaining.
Do not say handwriting is the sole permitted proof.

source_anchors.quote:
The burden shall be on the landlord to establish a knowing
and intentional election on the part of the tenant to repair the premises in compliance
with the applicable housing code. A mere recital in a form lease that tenant has covenanted
to repair will not be sufficient, it being the intention of this article that any
agreement with the tenant to repair be bargained for in fact. A separate hand-written
paragraph in the lease showing:
(1)
That the tenant has been informed of this article and the existing code violations;
(2)
That he/she has affirmatively elected and bargained to repair the violations listed
and other items listed; and
(3)
The inducement for such arrangements, will be prima facie evidence that such provision
was entered into in good faith and was bargained for in fact.

Stipulated facts: Tenant knew of the violations and the ordinance, intentionally elected to repair, and actually negotiated the listed repairs and reduction. cases.criterion: Recognize the stipulated bargaining facts; lack of handwriting alone is not dispositive. Keep city enforcement and the particular repair obligations separate.
must_not_infer: Do not reject the election solely because the paragraph is typed.
Do not declare every repair-cost transfer lawful.

cases.contract_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant. Synthetic facts for this diagnostic only: the dwelling is within Urbana city limits; this is an ordinary residential tenancy entered in 2026, and none of the supplied Chapter 12.5 section 2 exclusions applies. These are stipulated test facts, not a real boundary lookup. After tenancy termination, Landlord may immediately discard property reasonably believed to have a $5 sale value when storage would cost $100.
cases.criterion: Preserve the low-sale-value versus storage-cost immediate-disposal exception and its reasonable-belief condition.
must_not_infer: Do not say only valueless or perishable property qualifies.
Do not erase the reasonable-belief requirement.

source_anchors.quote:
If the tenant abandons the rental unit, the landlord may take possession of the rental
unit.
(c)
If the tenant abandons the rental unit or fails to remove his or her personal property
from the premises after termination of a rental agreement, the landlord shall leave
the abandoned property in the rental unit or remove and store all abandoned property
from the rental unit. The landlord may charge the tenant for the actual costs of storage.
The landlord may dispose of the property thirty (30) days after mailing written notice
to tenant's last known address, if the tenant does not claim the property within that
time. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the landlord reasonably believes such abandoned
property to be valueless or of such little value that the cost of storage would exceed
the amount that would be realized from sale, or if such property is subject to spoilage,
the landlord may immediately dispose of such property.

Stipulated facts: an identified nonperishable item has a $1000 sale value and $50 storage cost; there is no reasonable belief that it is valueless or low-value, and no notice has been mailed.

must_not_infer: Do not apply the low-value/perishable exception to these stipulated facts.

cases.contract_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant. Synthetic facts for this diagnostic only: the dwelling is within Urbana city limits; this is an ordinary residential tenancy entered in 2026, and none of the supplied Chapter 12.5 section 2 exclusions applies. These are stipulated test facts, not a real boundary lookup. For claimed damage beyond normal wear, Landlord will furnish an itemized estimated-cost statement within 30 days after Tenant vacates and paid receipts within 30 days of furnishing that statement.
cases.criterion: Recognize the estimated-statement then later-receipts path in the supplied municipal provision; do not reject it solely because receipts may arrive after day 30 from move-out.
must_not_infer: Do not require paid receipts in every case within 30 days of move-out.
Do not imply that all deductions are damage deductions.

source_anchors.quote:
If estimated cost is given, the lessor shall furnish the lessee with paid receipts,
or copies thereof, within thirty (30) days from the date the statement showing estimated
cost was furnished to the lessee, as required by this section. If no such statement
and receipts, or copies thereof, are furnished to the lessee as required by this section,
the lessor shall return the security deposit in full within forty-five (45) days of
the date that the lessee vacated the premises.

The deposit balance, if any, will be returned within 45 days after Tenant vacates.

Synthetic facts for this diagnostic only: the dwelling is within Urbana city limits; this is an ordinary residential tenancy entered in 2026, and none of the supplied Chapter 12.5 section 2 exclusions applies. These are stipulated test facts, not a real boundary lookup. Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $1,250. This agreement contains no other deposit-interest language. Deposit holding duration and payment history are not supplied.
cases.criterion: Describe interest language as absent, not an express waiver; identify duration and other required facts before claiming nonpayment.
must_not_infer: Do not invent an express waiver.
Do not infer that interest has not been paid from contractual silence.

source_anchors.quote:
A landlord who receives a security deposit of one hundred dollars ($100.00) or more
from a tenant to secure the payment of rent or to compensate for damage to property
shall pay interest to the tenant, computed from the date the deposit is paid, at a
rate equal to the interest paid by the largest commercial bank, as measured by total
assets, having its main banking premises in Champaign County, Illinois, on minimum
deposit passbook savings accounts as of the thirtieth of June immediately preceding
the inception of the rental agreement on any such deposit held by the landlord for
more than six (6) months.

cases.contract_text: RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT. Landlord leases a dwelling to Tenant. Synthetic facts for this diagnostic only: the dwelling is within Urbana city limits; this is an ordinary residential tenancy entered in 2026, and none of the supplied Chapter 12.5 section 2 exclusions applies. These are stipulated test facts, not a real boundary lookup. During the last 90 days, Landlord may show the dwelling at any time on a schedule determined only by Landlord. No non-renewal notice or other access facts are supplied.
cases.criterion: Identify the unilateral schedule and distinguish it from the conditional non-renewal showing exception; retain tenant-selected periods and unknown notice facts.
must_not_infer: Do not say every last-90-days showing automatically qualifies for notice-free access.

source_anchors.quote:
From the time that either the landlord or the tenant notifies the other party that
the rental agreement will not be renewed, the landlord shall have the right to access,
without twenty-four (24) hours advance notice, for the purpose of showing the rental
unit to prospective tenants, provided that:
(1)
The rental unit has not already been leased for the twelve-month period subsequent
to the expiration of the rental agreement;
(2)
The landlord enters only during two (2) specific one-hour periods on weekdays and
three (3) specific one-hour periods on weekends, selected by the tenant from among
choices offered by the landlord, during which the landlord will have daily access;
and
(3)
The landlord shall notify the tenant when the rental unit has been leased for the
twelve-month period subsequent to the expiration of the rental agreement.

Stipulated facts: a non-renewal notice was given, the dwelling has not been leased for the next 12 months, and Tenant selected two specific one-hour weekday periods and three one-hour weekend periods from choices Landlord offered. Showings will occur only during those periods; Landlord will notify Tenant when the next tenancy is leased.
cases.criterion: Recognize the stipulated showing exception conditions, without generalizing them to repairs or other entry purposes.
must_not_infer: Do not claim 24-hour notice is invariably required even for this supplied exception.
Do not convert the exception into unrestricted entry.
